children: By Janet H. Cho

Deckers Brands, maker of footwear brands including Hoka, Ugg, and Teva, lowered its revenue outlook for the year, sending its stock lower in after-hours trading despite reporting record revenue for the second quarter.
Deckers' stock was down 8% to $78.49 late Thursday afternoon, after closing down 0.3% at $85.28 in regular trading.

For its second fiscal quarter ended in September, Deckers said revenue rose 3.5% to a record $1.48 billion, its second straight quarter that revenue surpassed $1 billion. Diluted earnings rose to $2.31 a share, including 28 cents a share from Trump administration trade tariff refunds received in the quarter.
But investors were focused on its full fiscal year outlook for revenue of $5.7 billion to $5.75 billion.
That's down from its previous full-year guidance of $5.86 billion to $5.91 billion, issued as part of its first-quarter earnings on July 23.
Its first-quarter guidance said Hoka sales were expected to increase by a low-double-digit percentage year over year, and Ugg sales were expected to increase by a mid-single-digit percentage.

But its revised guidance now says Hoka sales are expected to increase by high-single-digit percentage from the previous year, while Ugg sales are projected to increase by a low-single-digit percentage.

President and CEO Stefano Caroti said Deckers delivered second-quarter earnings above its expectations by "maintaining disciplined marketplace management and a focus on expense control in a challenging consumer environment."

For the second half of fiscal 2027 that began Oct. 1, "we are taking deliberate actions to strengthen our connection with consumers, sharpen execution, and concentrate resources behind our greatest opportunities."

For the full fiscal year ending March 31, 2027, Deckers expects earnings of $7.80 to $7.95 a share. That includes a 52 cents a share gain from refunds received after the Supreme Court in February ruled that the Trump administration's use of the International Emergency Economic Powers Act to impose tariffs was illegal.
That's up from its previous guidance saying full-year EPS would be $7.35 to $7.50.
Customers have embraced Deckers' casual, well-cushioned, and high-performance footwear, apparel, and accessories, even if they know Hoka and Uggs better than the parent company.

Barron's on April 21 named Deckers as one of seven apparel and footwear retailer stocks where "consumer spending remains resilient," noting that while the company is facing higher costs, it has also lifted prices on some products, including "full-priced" Hoka sales.

For its second fiscal quarter, Deckers said Hoka brand net sales rose 6.8% to $677.2 million and Ugg sales rose 3.5% to $786.4 million, while other brands declined 54.3% to $17 million. Other brands include the phase-out of its Koolaburra brand standalone operations.
While domestic net sales declined 0.4% to $835.8 million, international net sales jumped 9% to $644.7 million.

Deckers repurchased about 3.2 million shares of its common stock in the quarter for $299.3 million at a weighted average price of $93.65. Fiscal year to date through Sept. 30, the Company repurchased approximately 6.5 million shares of its common stock for $637.5 million at a weighted average price of $98.77.
Deckers stock is down 17.7% year to date through Thursday's close and down 16.8% over the past 12 months.
